records.title: Ray: A Distributed Framework for Emerging AI Applications
records.reason: Ray is a general-purpose distributed framework for interactive AI applications. The paper's conclusion notes a training/serving/simulation loop, but the motivating applications and reported evaluation focus on reinforcement-learning workloads and distributed task throughput (up to 1.8 million tasks/s), not LLM inference or LLM-serving efficiency. General framework applicability alone does not establish the required LLM-inference focus, so this is unrelated to the assigned scope.

records.title: Megatron-LM: Training Multi-Billion Parameter Language Models Using Model Parallelism
records.reason: The primary source explicitly presents an intra-layer model-parallel method for training large Transformer models; experiments train models up to 8.3B parameters using 512 NVIDIA V100 GPUs (§1, §3-5). Its 15.1 PFLOP/s application throughput and 76% scaling efficiency describe distributed training. The conclusion's future work remains larger-scale pretraining and optimizer memory efficiency (§6). No inference-time efficiency method or evaluation is presented in the reviewed paper.

records.title: Blockwise Self-Attention for Long Document Understanding
records.reason: BlockBERT replaces dense self-attention with blockwise sparse attention and reports 27.8% lower inference time than RoBERTa at batch 8 and sequence length 1,024, with comparable QA accuracy. The evidence is for encoder-only BERT-family models and long-document QA rather than decoder-only LLM generation or serving. The attention idea is adjacent and potentially transferable, but the evaluated workload is outside core LLM inference, so it is retained as borderline.

records.title: Pollux: Co-adaptive Cluster Scheduling for Goodput-Optimized Deep Learning
records.reason: Pollux is explicitly a deep-learning cluster scheduler that jointly tunes resources, batch sizes and learning rates for distributed DL training jobs. Its goodput metric combines training system throughput and statistical efficiency; the experiments and conclusion address training-job scheduling, not LLM inference or serving. Excluded under the training-only scope rule.

records.title: LightSeq: A High Performance Inference Library for Sequence Processing and Generation
records.reason: LightSeq is an inference library for Transformer-family sequence generation that fuses GPU kernels, accelerates autoregressive/beam search, and reuses dynamic GPU memory. It reports up to 14x speedup over TensorFlow and 1.4x over FasterTransformer on machine-translation benchmarks; text-generation results are also compared. This is directly an inference performance library.

records.reason: Switch Transformers use sparse expert routing with roughly constant FLOPs per token, but the paper's main goal and measured speedups are pretraining scalability and training stability (up to 7x pretraining speed in its abstract). The manuscript evaluates training/fine-tuning quality and training regimes, not inference-serving efficiency or inference-time optimization. Under the workflow's training-only exclusion it is unrelated.

records.title: ZeroQuant: Efficient and Affordable Post-Training Quantization for Large-Scale Transformers
records.reason: ZeroQuant is an end-to-end quantization and inference pipeline combining hardware-friendly weight/activation quantization, affordable layerwise distillation and backend support to reduce quantization overhead. It reports INT8 inference gains up to 5.19x on BERT, 3.67x on GPT-J-6B, and reduced GPT-NeoX-20B latency from 65 ms to 25 ms while reducing inference GPUs from two to one. This directly optimizes model serving performance and memory.

records.title: LLM.int8(): 8-bit Matrix Multiplication for Transformers at Scale
records.reason: 行列積を8-bit化して大規模Transformerの推論memory footprintを削減する方式。本文はinference memoryを半減、BLOOM-176Bで1.96×削減を報告し、175B級checkpointをconsumer GPU環境で実行可能にする。速度向上は全体的に保証されず、小規模モデルではdequantization等によりslowdownする点を明示。

records.title: Petals: Collaborative Inference and Fine-tuning of Large Models
records.reason: Petals serves very large models collaboratively over heterogeneous participant resources, using 8-bit compression, server load balancing and low-latency client routing. It reports collaborative BLOOM-176B inference on consumer GPUs at approximately one step per second and states it outperforms RAM offloading for very large models. The work's direct subject includes collaborative LLM inference availability and latency.

records.title: Who Says Elephants Can't Run: Bringing Large Scale MoE Models into Cloud Scale Production
records.reason: The paper presents an MoE inference framework combining optimized kernels, routing and low-bit expert weights. It reports up to 26× throughput speedup over its PyTorch baseline and reduces model size to nearly one eighth of FP32 through 4-bit expert-weight quantization. The final focus is production inference serving of larger MoE models, making inference efficiency its direct objective.

records.title: SparseGPT: Massive Language Models Can be Accurately Pruned in One-Shot
records.reason: SparseGPT post-training prunes GPT-family models without retraining. On OPT-175B and BLOOM-176B it reports 50-60% sparsity with minor perplexity/zero-shot accuracy loss, including more than 100 billion weights ignored at inference. It also covers hardware-friendly 2:4 and 4:8 sparsity and sparsity-plus-quantization. This is model compression intended to lower LLM inference resource cost.

records.title: LLM-QAT: Data-Free Quantization Aware Training for Large Language Models
records.reason: Although quantization-aware training is the method, the produced low-bit LLMs target deployment efficiency: the paper quantizes weights, activations and KV cache, identifies KV-cache quantization as important for throughput and long sequences, and evaluates LLaMA 7B/13B/30B down to 4 bits. Its conclusion states accurate 4-bit LLM quantization is achievable and ties the method to the growing cost of LLM deployments. This meets the workflow rule allowing training as an internal method when the end goal is inference compression/efficiency.
